title: CAD finding
description: One finding as a CAD tool reports it in the tool-result envelope. The stable `code` is the rule identity (a later SARIF ruleId). `severity` is critical, major, minor or info

code.description: A stable finding code such as process.fdm.overhang or fit_unverified: lower-case words joined by underscores, optionally dotted into a namespace

severity.description: How bad the finding is, not whether it blocks: one shared blocking rule that every gate calls decides that, and under it minor and info are the non-blocking set. Canonical words only. Target mapping for the producers: error to major, layout stage to major or minor by layout_strict, no severity to major, warning to minor (warning is retired). That mapping keeps today's blocking effect only once the shared rule and the producers have migrated. Until then the only stand-alone same-effect mapping is warning to info

outcome.description: A check's result; unknown is never a pass, and not_assessed (calibration off, or no capability profile) is not a pass either

reason.description: Why a not_assessed finding was not assessed: its calibration is off, or no capability profile exists for it. Only a not_assessed finding carries one

subject.description: The part and feature the finding is about

location.description: Where in the project the finding applies: a project-relative file and, when known, a 1-based line

message.description: What is wrong, in one sentence

remedy.description: What to change to clear the finding

pointer.description: Where inside the document the finding applies, as the producer writes it, such as parts/0/rev

value.description: The offending or measured value, of any type

source.description: What produced the finding when the code alone does not say, such as step or kernel

examples.message: bore: H7 is a desired limit and no inspection verifies it
the overhang exceeds the printable angle
examples.remedy: add a chamfer or split the part
